$comment: Step order per platform. A step's `section` names a heading in a bundled doc, whose text scripts/generate.ts copies in; a missing heading fails generation. `quote` must appear in its file.

ios.title: Set up Yorozu on iPhone or iPad

steps.title: Install the Yorozu plugin on the computer that runs OpenClaw
steps.text: Yorozu needs your own OpenClaw Gateway (2026.9.8 or later). Run these on that computer, from a checkout of the Yorozu repository that will stay in place.

steps.title: Check the config (optional)
steps.text: Every key under channels.yorozu has a default, so no config is needed. Change `channels.yorozu.agent` to pick which agent answers. Use list_settings for every key.

steps.title: Install the app
steps.text: Install Yorozu from the App Store on the iPhone or iPad.

steps.title: Pair the device
steps.text: On the Gateway computer run `openclaw yorozu pair`, then in the app tap Scan QR Code and scan it. Check that the host key matches the fingerprint the command printed.

steps.title: Allow notifications
steps.text: The app asks right after pairing. Allowing it lets replies arrive as push notifications while the app is closed.

steps.title: Turn on voice input (optional)
steps.text: Settings › Voice Input downloads the on-device voice model from Apple (about 1.44 GB, on Wi-Fi unless you allow cellular). Needs iOS 26 or later and about 6 GB of RAM.

macos.title: Set up Yorozu on a Mac

steps.title: Install the Yorozu plugin on the computer that runs OpenClaw
steps.text: Yorozu needs your own OpenClaw Gateway (2026.9.8 or later). It can be this Mac or another computer. Run these on that computer, from a checkout of the Yorozu repository that will stay in place.

steps.title: Check the config (optional)
steps.text: Every key under channels.yorozu has a default, so no config is needed. Change `channels.yorozu.agent` to pick which agent answers. Use list_settings for every key.

steps.title: Install the app
steps.text: Download the signed, notarized DMG from https://yorozu.yumi.to/mac (the latest stable release) and drag Yorozu to Applications. It updates itself with Sparkle. To build from source instead, run `scripts/build_native.sh`.

steps.title: Pair the Mac
steps.text: On the Gateway computer run `openclaw yorozu pair` and paste the printed link into Pairing link, then click Pair. If an iPhone or iPad is already paired, you can instead scan the code the Mac shows from Settings › Add a Device › Scan a Mac's Code on that device.

steps.title: Allow notifications
steps.text: The app asks right after pairing. The Mac gets no push; while Yorozu runs, replies in other conversations post local notifications.

steps.title: Turn on voice input (optional)
steps.text: Settings › Voice Input downloads the on-device voice model from Hugging Face (about 1.44 GB, checked by SHA-256). macOS asks for the microphone the first time you record.
